## Console Errors Summary (distinct errors, all env-related)

1. **CORS/BLOCKED**: `8789/api/v1/projects/.../cells?side=target` — sync-worker not running or misconfigured; all cells-read operations fail. This is persistent and expected in this dev stack setup.
2. **500 on import**: `8789/import` — import worker endpoint returning 500; affects confirms for file uploads.
3. **500 on chat**: `8788/chat/api/v1/chat/completions` — OPENROUTER_API_KEY not configured; chat completions fail.
4. **403 on font**: `@fontsource-variable/geist` woff2 — Vite FS access restriction for node_modules font. Cosmetic (font fallback used).
5. **403 on admin**: `8788/api/v2/admin/me` — auth-worker admin endpoint returning 403 for non-admin user. Expected.
6. **500 on orgs/portfolio**: `8788/api/v2/orgs/25/portfolio` — server-side error on portfolio endpoint. Org 25 may not exist in this dev seed.
7. **[outbox-flush] server REJECTED events** — repeated; sync-worker rejecting outbox events due to CORS failure above.

**No JS crashes or unhandled exceptions. All errors are backend/env issues — no frontend JS errors.**

## Overall Verdict

**GO for promoting to main** — all 17 checks pass or are blocked only by known env limitations (server 500 on import confirm, CORS on sync-worker, missing AI key). No UI regressions found. The frontend code is clean.

### NEW BUGS (PD7 QA)

1. **Viewer role can still open and fully interact with the Import dialog.** Repro: seed a project member at role `viewer` (100), log in as them, open the project workspace, click the header "Import" button (or "More actions → Import" once a file is open). The full Import type-picker dialog opens with every importer (Upload files, eBible Corpus, Bible API, Spreadsheet, Macula, etc.) rendered fully clickable — nothing is disabled or hidden for a read-only role. Contrast with the same session's Voices panel, where "New voice" is correctly `[disabled]` for the same viewer. Not one of the 13 items in scope for this pass, but a clear miss of the "no import affordance for read-only roles" spirit of AQU-365. Files likely involved: wherever the header Import button / `ImportDialog` reads (or fails to read) the resolved project role — same `project.syncRole`/role-gating pattern as `RoleGatedStep`.
2. **`SYNC_WORKER_URL` missing/misrouted in every local dev-stack, silently defeating the AQU-346 live-eject notify.** `auth-worker/.dev.vars.example` has no `SYNC_WORKER_URL` entry at all (only `SYNC_SECRET_KEY`), and `auth-worker/wrangler.toml`'s `[env.e2e]` block sets `SYNC_WORKER_URL = "http://127.0.0.1:8788"` — that's auth-worker's own default port, not sync-worker's (8789 default / 8889 in this run). `notifySyncWorkerOfMemberRemoval` (`auth-worker/src/services/sync-worker-notify.ts`) early-returns when `SYNC_WORKER_URL` is falsy, so the ProjectSync DO is never told to eject a removed member's live WebSocket — the member-removal DELETE still 200s and the hard 403 guards (sync-token mint, POST /events membership re-check) still work, only the "instant live kick" UX is inert. Fix: add a correct `SYNC_WORKER_URL` (pointing at whatever port/URL sync-worker actually runs on) to `.dev.vars.example` and correct the `[env.e2e]` wrangler.toml value.
3. **AQU-347's "friendly no-op for the still-valid original redeemer" was never implemented, only "refuse after removal."** Repro: accept a single-use invite link as user A, then — while A is still a member — have A open the exact same `/join/<token>` link again. Expected (per the AQU-347 acceptance bar): a friendly redirect straight into the project (since A already has access). Actual: `GET /api/v2/invites/:token/preview` (`auth-worker/src/routes/invites.ts:208-240`) returns `410 {"error":"Invite already used","code":"used"}` whenever every row for that token has `used_at` set, with no special-case for `used_by === the current caller` — so the join page renders a hard "This link has already been used… ask for a new invite link" error even for the person who redeemed it seconds ago. The POST accept route (lines ~352-382) does have same-user-reaccept-is-a-noop logic, but the GET preview page 410s before accept is ever attempted, so a still-valid member can never reach it via a repeat click. Fix: have the preview endpoint check `used_by === caller.id` (when the caller is authenticated) and return a "already yours, continue" shape instead of the generic `used` 410.
4. **AQU-334 role gate for the Project Setup checklist doesn't fire for a real sub-floor contributor.** Repro: as a project member at role 400 (contributor) — bob in the dev seed — open the "Setup: N/4" checklist. Expected: "Set translation instructions" / "Invite collaborators" / "Configure voice & transcription" render read-only with a lock icon + role-naming tooltip (per `RoleGatedStep`'s own doc comment and the AQU-334 commit message). Actual: all four steps render fully enabled, confirmed via DOM inspection (`[data-testid="role-gated-step"]` count = 0) across 4 independent fresh page loads, even though the server-side `GET /api/v2/projects/dev-project` correctly reports `role.level = 400` for this user. `RoleGatedStep`'s gating math is correct in isolation and treats `roleLevel == null` as an intentional bypass (documented for unsynced/local-only projects) — so the likely defect is that `SetupChecklistDrawer`'s `project.syncRole?.level` is resolving to `null`/undefined at the point the checklist renders for a non-owner, despite `minimalProjectRecord` (`src/lib/sync/cloud-projects.ts:200-227`) correctly mapping the server's `role` field to `syncRole`. `ProjectWorkspace.tsx`'s `hydratedProject = clientProject ?? loadedProject` (line 257) is a plausible culprit worth checking first — if `clientProject` is ever non-null without a `syncRole` field, it would silently defeat the gate for every project member, not just bob. Needs a dedicated debugging session; not fixed here per QA scope.

#### AQU-347 second re-verify (client half landed, @ 3a8efa22c)

Stack fully restarted again (required: vite's watcher had missed the git-driven change — the bare-URL curl check showed fresh source while the browser's `?t=`-stamped module graph still ran the pre-3a8efa22c code; after restart the build badge read `3a8efa2` and the new request pattern appeared). Served-code fingerprints confirmed before testing: `previewMultiInvite` in the served module carries the `Authorization: Bearer ${jwt}` logic, and `JoinPage.tsx` passes `session?.jwt ?? null` with `session?.jwt` in the effect deps.

**AQU-347 — still FAIL end-to-end in a default browser, but the remaining defect is now a single caching gap, fully isolated:**

- The client fix **works as designed**: on the still-member redeemer's re-click, the preview fires twice unauthenticated (StrictMode double-mount before session hydration), then re-fires **with** the Authorization header once the session loads — observed live.
- The server logic **works as designed**: the browser's exact JWT replayed via curl returns `200 {usedByCaller: true}`; post-removal it correctly 410s.
- **The killer: HTTP response caching.** The preview endpoint's responses carry only `Vary: Origin` — no `Cache-Control: no-store`, no `Vary: Authorization` — and a 410 is heuristically cacheable (RFC 9110 §15.5.11). Within a single page load, the first (unauthenticated, pre-session-hydration) request receives a real 410 which Chrome caches; when the session hydrates and the effect re-fires with auth, **Chrome serves the cached 410 without hitting the server** — confirmed by the identity worker log: the authed GET's CORS preflight (OPTIONS) reaches the server but the GET itself never does, and Playwright reports a 410 the server never sent for that request. Reproduced identically in a brand-new browser context (fresh cache — the poisoning happens within one page load, so every re-click load self-defeats).
- **Proof the rest of the chain is correct:** re-running the identical flow with Playwright route interception on the preview URLs (which bypasses the browser HTTP cache) produces 410 → 410 → authed **200**, the friendly **"You're invited … Accept invitation"** confirm card renders (no dead-link error), and clicking Accept lands in `/project/dev-project`. The intended AQU-347 UX is one cache header away from working.
- **Smallest fixes (any one suffices):** (a) client: add `cache: "no-store"` to the `previewMultiInvite`/`previewServerInvite` fetch options; (b) server: send `Cache-Control: no-store` (or `private, no-cache`) on the invite-preview responses; (c) client: gate the first preview on `!sessionLoading` so the unauth 410 is never requested (and cached) in the first place — (a)+(b) together is the robust choice.

**Updated re-verify summary: AQU-334 PASS · AQU-346 PASS · AQU-347 FAIL (default-browser) — client+server halves both verified correct; blocked solely by a heuristically-cached unauth 410 (missing `no-store` on the preview request/response); works end-to-end with cache bypassed.**
